name: Ear training

lead: Ear training teaches you to recognise pitches, intervals, melodies and rhythms by ear. In voice discussions it is borrowed to build awareness of vocal pitch and a more intentional tone.

It is a core part of formal music education, using solfege, interval and chord recognition, rhythm exercises and apps. Its use for voice appearance is anecdotal, and no studies have tested it for attractiveness outcomes.

paras: People do short listening and identification exercises with apps or a teacher, then try to match and control pitch with their own voice.

angle.text: Learning to recognise pitches by ear gives better awareness and control of your own vocal pitch, for a more intentional voice tone. It is established for music skills and borrowed for voice.

lead: Ear training is the practice of learning to recognize pitches, intervals, melodies, chords and rhythms by ear alone, a core part of formal music education.[1] In looksmaxxing-adjacent voice discussions it is mentioned for pitch awareness, for example controlling vocal pitch.

Methods include solfege, interval and chord recognition, rhythm exercises and software or apps.[1] One study reported that musical ear training was examined in cochlear implant users for speech and music perception.[2] No studies have tested ear training for appearance or attractiveness outcomes.

paras: No studies found for appearance uses. Studies of related populations include a study of musical ear training in cochlear implant users.[2] A 2017 study examined thresholds for discriminating melodic pitch intervals.[3]
